hints: Ask yourself, has a newborn baby had time to meet pathogens and make its own antibodies yet, or must the antibodies have come from someone else?
Remember, passive means receiving ready-made antibodies, and natural means no human medical injection was involved, just mother to baby via placenta and breast milk.
walkthrough:
**Active or Passive?**

Think of it simply. Active means YOU make your own antibodies after meeting an antigen. Passive means you are GIVEN ready-made antibodies from someone else.

A newborn has not had infections or vaccines yet, so it cannot have made its own antibodies. It must have been given them.

**Natural or Artificial?**

Natural means it happens by nature with no medical help. Artificial means it involves human medicine like a vaccine or an injection of antibodies.

At birth, antibodies pass naturally across the placenta and later in breast milk (mainly IgG and IgA). No doctor gave an injection.

**Put It Together**

Given antibodies from another person = passive. Happening naturally from mother = natural.

So the baby has passive natural immunity, which is short-lived but vital protection in the first months.

options.A: Active artificial needs the baby to make its own antibodies after vaccination, which has not happened at birth.
options.B: Active natural needs the baby to catch an infection and make its own memory cells, which has not happened at birth.
options.C: Passive is correct because antibodies are received, but artificial is wrong because no injection of antibodies was given.
options.D: Correct, as ready-made maternal antibodies are passed naturally via the placenta and breast milk, giving short-term passive natural immunity.
